production.note: Calendar build years (home market). Aston Martin's media site gives '2010-2012'; Aston's own past-models page (am-one-77-past-model) says produced 2009-2012, counting from the 2009 reveal; Aston's release reproduced by Zercustoms (zercustoms-one-77-release) says 'The first deliveries will begin in early 2011'; Evo's panel (evo-one-77-a-z) gives 'Years made 2011-12'. 77 cars.

body.note: Two-seat coupe ('carbon fibre monocoque clad in a seamless bodyshell').

configuration.note: '7312 cc V12, Alloy quad overhead camshaft, 48-valve'

displacementL.note: 7,312 cc (Aston: '7312 cc V12'). Evo's panel prints '7299cc' (evo-one-77-a-z); both round to 7.3.

aspiration.note: 'the most powerful naturally aspirated road car engine in the world today'

drivetrain.note: Front-mid V12 with a 'Rear mid-mounted, six-speed automated manual gearbox' (rear transaxle), i.e. rear-wheel drive.

transmission.note: 'Rear mid-mounted, six-speed automated manual gearbox with auto shift manual/select shift manual (ASM/SSM) electric hydraulic control system'. The same page also carries a generic line '6-speed manual with optional 5-speed automatic', which contradicts this and every other source and is treated as a template error. Top Gear: 'robotised six-speed, single-clutch manual, with paddleshifters' (topgear-one-77-driving).

powerHp.note: Quote (Aston Martin press release reproduced by Zercustoms): "The 7.3 liter V12 engine, as part of the development process, has been certified at 750bhp and 750Nm of torque, positioning it as the most powerful naturally aspirated road car engine in the world today." Aston stated the rating in bhp, so it is used as published (powerStandard Other). Evo's panel (evo-one-77-a-z): 'Max power 750bhp'; Top Gear (topgear-one-77-review): 'Rated at 750bhp and 553lb ft'. Aston's 2009 reveal release promised 'no less than 700 bhp' (pre-production).

weightLb.note: Step 1 of the weight order (manufacturer figure). Quote (Aston Martin past-models page): "1630 kg" under the heading Weight, with no kerb or dry label. 1,630 kg x 2.20462 = 3,593.5 lb, rounded to 3,594. Top Gear (topgear-one-77-driving): 'it weighs 1,630kg'. Read as a kerb weight because Aston and Top Gear give it without a dry label; Aston's 2009 reveal release gave 'a projected weight of 1,500 kg' (see discrepancies).
